The update rewrites the refill step in TokenBucket.consume: it captures the elapsed time, guards against negative elapsed values (which could occur from NTP clock corrections) by clamping them to zero, adds tokens based on the bounded elapsed time, and explicitly caps the token count at the bucket’s capacity. This prevents the bucket from unintentionally emptying or exceeding its limit, ensuring stable rate‑limiting behavior.

The update adds robust time handling and capacity clamping to the token bucket. It stores elapsed time in a variable, prevents negative elapsed values (which could empty the bucket during clock rollback), and caps tokens at the maximum capacity after refill. The previous single‑line min() call is replaced with explicit logic for clarity and safety.

The diff adds robust handling for time regression in the token bucket rate limiter. It captures elapsed time in a variable, clamps negative elapsed values to zero to avoid draining tokens when clocks move backward, and then updates tokens. It also ensures tokens never exceed capacity by capping after refill. This prevents lockouts caused by NTP adjustments and keeps the bucket’s token count accurate.

It controls request rate by replenishing tokens at a fixed rate; each request consumes a token, allowing bursts up to bucket capacity, then throttling excess traffic.
Token bucket limits request rate by storing tokens; each request consumes a token. Tokens refill at a set rate, allowing bursts up to bucket capacity.
A token bucket rate limiter controls request flow by storing tokens that refill over time; each request consumes a token, allowing bursts up to bucket capacity while limiting average rate.
